newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay makes no forecast for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Solvay makes no forecast for 1997.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA on Thursday would make no forecast for earnings in 1997 after current net 1996 profits before exceptionals fell eight percent to 11.5 billion Belgian francs.

"I would not like to make any forecasts for 1997 whatsoever....(but) I am certainly hoping that 1997 current profits will return to the 1995 level," chief executive officer Daniel Janssen told a news conference on provisional 1996 results. In 1995 Solvay had net current earnings of 12.5 billion francs.
Hopes for 1997 were in part centred on an expected continuation of a recovery for PVC and high-density poly-ethylene prices, he said.

Together with polypropylene the two products make up the plastics sector, where results dropped by more than 50 percent in 1996. The sector accounts for about 30 percent of group sales, which totalled 282.7 billion francs ($8.83 billion) in 1996. Janssen said Solvay expected its health sector -- the second most important contributor to 1996 profits -- to grow more rapidly than the rest of the group this year. "We will try and accelerate growth through acquisitions in the U.S."
Solvay will use the proceeds from the 1996 sale of its animal health business -- about 14 billion francs, or $450 million -- for investments in the health sector.

Total sales in human health products grew by 12 percent in 1996, faster than group sales, which increased by three percent. U.S. sales of compulsive disorder drug Fluvoxamine more than doubled since 1995.
Drugs account for 16 to 17 percent of group sales, Janssen said and 60 percent of total research spending.
